title: Frequency of Elements
directAnswer: Iterate once, doing `count[x] = count.getOrDefault(x, 0) + 1`. The map is the frequency table. O(n) time, O(k) space.

remember.takeaway: The frequency map is the most reused fresher-to-advanced primitive.

problemStatement: Given an integer array `nums`, return a map from each value to how many times it appears.
understanding: A hash map keyed by value, incrementing the count for each element.

approaches.name: Hash map counting
approaches.whenToMention: This is the standard, expected solution — lead with it.
approaches.explanation:
Build a **frequency map**: a hash map from each value to its count, filled in a single pass with `count[x] = count.getOrDefault(x, 0) + 1`. This table is the single most reused primitive from fresher problems all the way to hard ones.

**Why getOrDefault / Counter.** The first time you see a value it has no entry; `getOrDefault(x, 0)` (Java) or `collections.Counter` (Python) supplies the implicit 0 so you don't NullPointer or KeyError on first sight.

**Why O(n) time, O(k) space.** One pass over n elements, each an O(1) map update; the map holds k distinct keys, so space is O(k) ≤ O(n).

**Why it matters.** Anagram checks, top-K frequent, majority element, group-by, and first-unique-character all reduce to building this map first. Learn the increment idiom cold and a whole family of problems opens up.
hints: What structure maps a value to a running count?
Increment count[x], defaulting to 0 for first sightings.
This same map powers anagrams, top-K, and majority element.
approaches.insight: This single building block unlocks a huge family of harder problems — learn it cold.
approaches.complexityReasoning: one O(1) map update per element (O(n) total); the map stores k ≤ n distinct keys.

java.explanation: Increment the bucket, defaulting to 0 for first sightings.

pitfalls: Forgetting the default for a first appearance (NullPointerException in Java).
Scanning a list per value (O(n²)) instead of one map pass.

commonMistakes: Forgetting the default for a value's first appearance (NullPointerException).
Using a list and scanning it (O(n²)).

clarifyingQuestions.question: Return a map or sorted counts?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: A value→count map; I can post-process for top-K or sorting.

commonMistakesDetailed.title: No default on first sight
commonMistakesDetailed.why: `freq.get(x) + 1` throws when x is absent (null in Java). Use getOrDefault / Counter so first sightings start at 0.
commonMistakesDetailed.bad: freq.put(x, freq.get(x) + 1);            // NPE when x is new
